extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars and researchers in sociology/criminology/race studies; policymakers interested in policing, crime statistics and race relations
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-sociological guidance for analysing 'mugging', crime statistics, media/political responses, and the structural position of black labour and youth in urban Britain. Emphasises contextual, structural and qualitative inquiry over isolated quantitative readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not isolate crime indices from related indices
rubrics_metrics.description: 'This crime index cannot be isolated from other related indices if we really wish to unravel this puzzle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat crime figures as part of a broader set of social indicators (employment, housing, education, political context). Avoid reading isolated crime statistics as self-explanatory; they require cross-index comparison to understand causes and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize crime figures within economic, social and political crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: When examined in context, these various indices point to a critical intersection between black crime, black labour and the deteriorating situation in the black areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse increases in crime alongside local economic decline, unemployment, and political trends; consider how recession and policy choices produce conditions that shape criminal activity and its interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer structural and qualitative investigation over merely statistical interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The shift, then, is not statistical but qualitative. It is a matter for structural, not quantitative investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask how structural changes (labour markets, segregation, school reproduction) alter social relations and behaviours rather than only computing rates and percentages. Use qualitative methods and theory to interpret statistical change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localise the problem to class fraction and specific areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The most salient feature of this qualitative shift is the localising of the problem. 'Mugging' is now unquestionably identified with a specific class fraction or category of labour (black youth) and with a specific kind of area: the inner-ring zones of multiple deprivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing crime to groups, examine spatial concentration and class composition: inner-city ‘trouble spots’, zones of multiple deprivation, and their relation to unemployment and service decline. Avoid generalized attributions across whole populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine education's role in reproducing labour position and 'secondariness'
rubrics_metrics.description: It is above all the school and the education system which has the principal function of 'skilling' the different sectors of the working class selectively and assigning blacks to their rough positions in the hierarchy of occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how curricula, teacher attitudes, tracking, and institutional culture channel minority youth into low-skilled occupational paths. Consider 'reproduction of the worker' frameworks and how schools can generate compliance or resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat discrimination as structural and routine rather than as isolated exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: But the measuring of discrimination...gives a false picture; for it treats racism and discriminatory practices as individual exceptions to an otherwise satisfactory 'rule'. Instead we want to examine what the regular and routine structures are and what their effects have been.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should map recurrent institutional practices (housing allocation, labour market segmentation, educational curricula) that systematically disadvantage minorities, not only count overt discriminatory acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse language and cultural capital in educational disadvantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Language is the prin[bearer] of cultural capital...Measures which could formally be designed to develop additional competences in the spoken and written language...frequently become, instead, the means by which existing linguistic competences are dismantled and expropriated - as 'poor speech'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In assessing schooling effects, examine how standard-language policies, misrecognition of home languages/dialects, and curricular omissions devalue students' cultural capital. Look for both unintended and deliberate processes that label nonstandard speech as substandard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege community and social-worker observations where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Black community and social workers in these areas believe this to be the case, an impression more reliable than the figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat local organisational and community testimony as valuable evidence, especially where official statistics are unreliable or politically framed. Use such qualitative insights to correct or nuance quantitative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critically interrogate media and political narratives that construct moral panics
rubrics_metrics.description: The spectre of a new 'flood' of displaced Asians set in motion a new wave of reaction...the panic response...systematically articulated by sections of the national press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how newspapers, politicians and public figures frame immigration and crime (scapegoating, sensational headlines, leaked reports) to produce moral panics. Examine stories, metaphors (floods, invasion), and the political uses of such narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question criminological/statistical computation, especially ethnic highlighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures computed as these were, and released in this form (a form which later attracted the censure of Sir Robert Mark himself for unduly highlighting the ethnic element)...provided the 'hard' quantitative basis for spirals of moral concern...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize how crime statistics are aggregated, coded and released; detect selection or emphasis (e.g., ethnic breakdowns) that may amplify moral panic. Consider official critiques and methodological weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse policing as crisis management and social control
rubrics_metrics.description: Crises have to be remedied, their worst effects contained or mitigated. They also have to be controlled. To put it crudely, they have to be policed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how policing priorities, rhetoric and deployment change during crises to maintain order, often at the expense of marginalised communities. Consider police self-positioning as 'keepers of the peace' and their shifting discourse toward social-economic dimensions of crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map occupational concentration and sectoral distribution of black labour to explain exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Black labour is heavily concentrated in some sectors of engineering, in foundry work, in textiles, as general labourers...Three types of work are characteristic...small-scale productive labour in sweat-shop conditions...lengthy hours...highly mechanised...assembly-line types of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining socioeconomic position and propensity to unemployment or marginalisation, document the sectoral distribution of work, job types, unionisation rates, shift-work prevalence, and how these shape vulnerability to recession and exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate immigrant labour flows to capital needs and legislative regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: What has principally governed the 'flow' of black labour is the underlying rhythms and requirements of British capital. But what has regulated the flow is, of course, legislative (i.e. political) action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse immigration and labour policies as instruments that tune labour supply to capital's needs (e.g., restrictions on dependants, guest-worker regimes). Examine how legislation, capitalist demand, and racial ideology interact to produce flexible, exploitable labour pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: See crime statistics as part of a politically produced spiral rather than purely evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures...provided the 'hard' quantitative basis for spirals of moral concern and corrective control, whatever their factual base, and rapidly became a part of the spiral they purported to explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to feedback loops where figures justify controls which then alter social conditions and subsequent figures. Evaluate claims about cause/effect critically and trace political consequences of statistical releases.
